name: Shellac
aliases: E904, shellac, bleached shellac, goma laca, laca blanqueada
what_is: A resin secreted by lac insects and purified for use as a glossy food coating.
why_botia: Shellac is the resin secreted by an insect, and it is used as a glossy coating on fruit, sweets and dragées. It is barely digested, and JECFA found no concern with its use as an external coating. Because of its origin, BOTIA flags it for people choosing vegan, halal or kosher food — the international halal standard BOTIA follows does not allow insects. And on fresh fruit it does not appear on any label.
can_1: Identify E904, shellac or bleached shellac when declared on an ingredient list.
can_2: Explain its insect origin and glazing function and show the Animal, Muslim, Texture and E-number layers.
cannot_1: Determine from an unlabelled piece of fresh fruit whether shellac or another glazing treatment was used.
cannot_2: Determine the amount, coating thickness or exact shellac grade from the ingredient name alone.

title: Shellac
description: Shellac (E904) is an insect-secreted resin used as a glossy coating on fruit and confectionery; its insect origin matters for vegan, halal and kosher traceability.
